# Review — bardo-thodol-002 (pp. 18–26)

## Pass 1

Read against conventions.md, packet.md (print, fixes, establishment log), units.py / bardo-thodol-001.json
(pilot), glossary.json and run3/RUNBOOK.md "Reviewer". 50 units checked word by word. LETTERS OK after the
changes (one division change, unit 34).

### Changes

- unit 1 · l · minor · "lion's lying-posture": 'dug stangs is "manner of sitting / posture", nothing says lying · now "lion's posture".
- unit 1 · n · minor · rtsir ba → btsir ba was presented as a reading ("taken as"), not plainly as a guess · note now says it is read as a guess and the translation rests on it.
- unit 2 · l · style · "The sleep two channels" broke Tibetan order (gnyid log rtsa gnyis) and differed from unit 24 · now "Sleep channels two".
- unit 2 · n · minor · the sense of 'phar 'phro chad was stated as fact; it is built from the parts · note now says it is a guess.
- unit 3 · l · minor · "path-by" for lam du (terminative, not instrumental) · now "path-along".
- unit 3 · l, n · style · "dhūti" vs the pilot's "dhūtī" · English form brought into line with the pilot; note now says the print writes dhu ti without length marks.
- unit 4 · l · style · "reality-itself's clear-light" added a genitive the Tibetan lacks (chos nyid 'od gsal) · now "reality-itself clear-light".
- unit 6 · l, n · style · "avadhūti" · now "avadhūtī", as the pilot's note names it (the note still says the print leaves the last i short).
- unit 15 · l · style · "near's that-at" garbled khad pa der · now "near being, at-that".
- unit 16 · i · minor · "Begin with 'O child…', or, if it is a lama: 'Honoured sir, please keep your resolve undistracted.' Say this…" invented "begin with" and tied the request to the lama case only; the Tibetan is address (rigs kyi bu, or drung pa lags for a lama) + request + zhes snyan du … zhus · rebuilt: "Say softly into the ear: 'O child of noble family', or, if it is a lama, 'Honoured sir', and then 'please keep your resolve undistracted.'"
- unit 16 · n · minor · skad chung dus given as "probably" without saying the print is kept and the reading is a guess · note now says so plainly.
- unit 23 · n · style · "mi 'jug par, 'not letting (him) go'" lost the object of 'jug (yengs su) · now "yengs su mi 'jug par, 'not letting (him) go into distraction'".
- unit 27 · n · minor · ཨང "seems to be" a cry — not plainly called a guess · now "ang is uncertain: it is taken, as a guess, for…".
- unit 29 · n · minor · phyal chad: the sense was not plainly called a guess · now says the sense given is a guess.
- unit 30 · n · minor · grammatical label: "dbyer, 'to separate'" — dbyer is dbye (noun / future stem of 'byed) + -r, not a verb "to separate" · corrected; phyed now "a form of the same verb".
- unit 31 · i · minor · skye shi med pa is an attribute of the buddha 'Od mi 'gyur ba, not the predicate of awareness ("has neither birth nor death: it is also…") · rebuilt: "…abiding as a great mass of light: this very thing is also the buddha Unchanging Light, who has neither birth nor death."
- unit 32 · l, i · minor · rang gi rig pa la rang lta ba = oneself looking at one's own awareness; l was ambiguous and i made awareness the subject ("awareness looking at itself") · l "one's-own knowing at, oneself looking it-is"; i "that is you yourself looking at your own awareness".
- unit 34 · w · minor · division: འོད་གསལ་ དུ་ separate, though du governs the single noun 'od gsal (pilot attaches su/du/tu to a single noun: མདུན་དུ, མཚམས་སུ, and this draft's སངས་རྒྱས་སུ in unit 32; it separates only after a phrase: གཡས་ གཡོན་ དུ, འོད་གསལ་ སྤྲོས་བྲལ་ དུ) · now འོད་གསལ་དུ་. LETTERS OK.
- unit 34 · i · minor · "becomes the body of truth, never to meet or part from it" is self-contradictory for chos sku 'du 'bral med par gyur · now "becomes one with the body of truth, beyond meeting and parting".
- unit 34 · n · minor · rang gi shes nas was called "thin" but the translation was not plainly called uncertain · added "and is uncertain".
- unit 42 · n · minor · rdzogs rim par yin na: the stray -r was noted but its effect on the reading not stated · note now says the sense is uncertain and the translation passes over it.
- unit 43 · l · style · "the visualisation read" was interpretive in the literal layer · now "the clear-realisation read" (mngon rtogs; the note explains it).
- unit 45 · n · minor · "the other recension is corrupt" overstated the log ("corrupt or different") · now gives its reading gdos bcos ma su, "perhaps a corruption".

Severity count: major 0 · minor 16 · style 7 (23 change lines).

### Checked and confirmed (no change)

- Verb stems the drafter asked about, all correct: mnan past of gnon (gnon/mnan/gnan/non); phab past of 'bebs ('bebs/phab/dbab/phob); btang past of gtong; bzhag past of 'jog (imp. zhog); bos past of 'bod; zhus past of zhu; shar past of 'char; gtad past of gtod; klogs imperative of klog (klog/bklags/bklag/klogs); sgoms imperative of sgom (sgom/bsgoms/bsgom/sgoms); nyon imperative of nyan. Also gdab future of 'debs (u. 4), ngo sprad past of ngo sprod (u. 42), byas past of byed (u. 1).
- ces after final g: units 23, 45, 46 all follow ཅིག / ཤིག — correct; zhes after vowels elsewhere — correct. Imperative particle cig / shig: gtod cig (d), sgoms shig, yengs shig (s) — correct.
- Genitive / instrumental allomorphs in w: ཀུན་ གྱི, ཐོན་ གྱི, འདུལ་ གྱི, བདུན་ གྱི, ཉམས་ལེན་ གྱི (after n/l); རྩ་རླུང་ གི, གོང་ གི, མཆོག་ གི, ཚངས་བུག་ གི (after ng/g); ཚིག་ གིས, ཕལ་པ་ རྣམས་ ཀྱིས (after g/s) — all regular.
- Misprint fixes named in their units in the required form: མཆད (6), ཉམས་ལན (26), མཚན་མཁ་དོག (28), ཤོར་བདང (50). Abbreviations / contractions written out and named: གྶི, ནམཁའ (18), ཅནྡུ, སྒོཾས (45), འདེབྶ (48), དགོསོ (50). Every [?] (re, 11; shig and ལན, 26; sing nga, 29; ཅནྡུ, 45) is called uncertain. The interlinear addition (26) is described.
- Other-recension differences of sense from the log are all mentioned: units 3, 4, 7, 11, 17, 18, 25, 29, 31, 33, 34, 40, 41, 45.
- House renderings: the between / bardo, face-introduce / point out, clear light, reality-itself / reality, body of truth, knowing / awareness, wind, channel — consistent throughout.
- No phrase in i reads as a remembered published translation (no "O nobly born", etc.); the i's are built from the grammar.

### Findings considered and refused

- Division གསལ་གདབ / གསལ་བཏབ / གསལ་འདེབས as one word: kept. The pilot writes གསལ་འདེབས་ as one word (title, u. 1, 19); the verb is lexicalised. Where a negative intervenes it is split (གསལ་ མི་ ཐེབས, u. 48), correctly.
- ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྐུ, ཀུན་ཏུ་བཟང་མོ / པོ, འོད་མི་འགྱུར་བ as one word: kept. The pilot keeps names and lexical compounds with an internal particle whole (རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ, དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པ, དེ་མ་ཐག་ཏུ, པདྨ་འབྱུང་གནས).
- ཅི་ནས་ཀྱང one word: kept, like the pilot's གང་ཡང (lexical adverb), while free ཀྱང / ཡང after a word stay separate, as in the draft.
- ཞེས་པའམ one word: kept; -pa is the nominaliser on zhes, and -'am is fused, like the pilot's བླ་མའམ.
- གདོས་བཅས་ཅན་དུ one word: kept; can is a suffix and du follows a single word.
- ཕྱལ་ཆད་དུ attached: kept; du governs the single noun phyal chad (stong pa is the subject).
- ལམ་གྱིས (u. 37, "in a flash", as the pilot's u. 26) vs ལམ་ གྱིས (u. 50, "by the path"): kept. Different words: in u. 50 "in a flash" gives no sense with goms 'dris yod; the note there says so.
- rigs kyi bu in l as "child-of-noble-family" where the pilot's l has "Child of the family": kept, because conventions.md gives "child of noble family" as the house rendering without distinguishing layers; flagged for QUESTIONS.
- klogs te (u. 43): imperative followed by te is unusual, but klogs is the imperative stem and instructional prose runs on this way; label kept.
- mnan no (u. 2) as an instruction in the past stem: the note already says so; kept.
- rang gi thub na (u. 13) read as gi for gis: kept; it is the print's habit the pilot and conventions record (གཅིག་གི for གིས), and the sense is unaffected.
- u. 5 i leaves gcig ("one, a single") unrendered: idiomatic layer; l has it. Kept.
- u. 40 i "hears their crying" for du rgod (prob. ngu rgod "weeping and laughter"): the note says the reading is uncertain and that the translation takes it as crying; kept.
- u. 2 alternative sense (the pressing cuts off the throbbing): chad is intransitive, so "having stopped" is the natural reading; kept, with the guess now flagged.
- u. 15 phog par bya: no stem label given in the note, and "make it land" is a fair rendering; kept.
- u. 36 note "cig is gcig in its softened form": kept; after n the indefinite would be zhig, so this is the numeral gcig without its prefix, as the note says.
- u. 18 thugs bskyed (honorific) in the mouth of bdag: the note already says the formula keeps it; kept.

## Pass 2

Second pass: every one of the 289 entries in gloss.json checked against its word and its use in units.json, the master glossary's
style and the pilot; then all 50 units read again from the original through `l` to `i`. Both files were edited by script.
`w` is unchanged, and LETTERS OK (50 units). There was no division change, so the key set is the same: all 289 keys in
novel-forms.json have an entry in gloss.json, and there are no extra entries.

### Changes: gloss.json

- gloss རིམ་བ / གསལ་བཏབ · entry · major · the two entries were swapped (རིམ་བ was glossed "made clear (gsal + btab)", and གསལ་བཏབ "order, order of steps (rim ba…)") · each now has its own sense: rim ba "order, succession, stage (the print's spelling of rim pa)"; gsal btab "made clear, reminded (btab, past of 'debs; the past of gsal 'debs)".
- gloss ཟིན · stem · major · "('dzin 'hold'; zin past)": zin is not a stem of 'dzin (the past of 'dzin is bzung); it is the intransitive verb beside it · now "(zin, the intransitive verb beside 'dzin 'to hold')".
- gloss ཟིན་པ, ཟིན་པའི, ཟིན་པར · stem · minor · these repeated the 'dzin/zin claim, or gave "seize" as transitive · corrected in the same way, each with its use (ngos mi zin pa, dran pas mi zin pa'i, zin par the tshom med).
- gloss ཤེས་རིགས · entry · minor · "read shes rig, with rigs for rig" did not say what the letters are or why the s stands. The print writes ཤེས་རིག everywhere else in this part (u. 28–30), so this is a one-off form, not a spelling habit · now: shes rig printed once with a final s, which the following kyi agrees with; the print elsewhere writes shes rig, and it is read so.
- gloss རིགས་པ · entry · minor · "(rigs pa as printed; read rig pa)": the same problem. Also, rigs pa is a real word ("reasoning, what is fitting"), and the reader should be told that it does not fit here · rewritten on the same lines as ཤེས་རིགས, and the real word is named.
- gloss ཅིག · sense · minor · "also the command particle cig 'do!' after a verb": in this division, cig as a command is always fused (མཛོད་ཅིག, ཉོན་ཅིག, གཏོད་ཅིག). The free word ཅིག comes only in u. 36 (ཟན་ ཅིག་ ཟ), where it is gcig, "a, one" · the command sense is removed; the entry is now "one, a (gcig written without its prefix g-)".
- gloss ཨང · entry · minor · "(ang; reading a guess)": the letters are clear; what is a guess is the sense · now "the letters are clear, the sense is not; taken, as a guess, for a spoken cry…". In line with the note to u. 27.
- gloss ཡུད་པ · entry · minor · "reading uncertain" put the doubt on yud pa, but the [?] in u. 11 is on the re that follows it · the doubt is removed, and the entry now reads "a moment (yud, as in yud tsam, + -pa)".
- gloss འཕར་འཕྲོ · Wylie of parts · minor · "(rbar 'phar 'leap' + 'phro…)": the form "rbar 'phar" is invented; the key is 'phar 'phro · now "('phar 'to throb, to leap' + 'phro 'what is still going on')", and the sense of 'phar 'phro chad is called a guess, as in the note to u. 2.
- gloss རྩིར་བ · entry · minor · the guess was mixed in with the gloss ("a pressing, to press (… perhaps a mistake … uncertain; + -ba)") · now "as printed rtsir ba, not a known verb; read, as a guess, as btsir ba 'to press'", as in the note to u. 1.
- gloss སྐད་ཆུང · entry · minor · the entry said "perhaps" and gave "softly", without saying that the translation's reading is a guess · now names the print's skad chung dus and says it is read, as a guess, as skad chung du (u. 16).
- gloss དུ་རྒོད · entry · minor · "weeping(?) and laughing(?) … the sense 'crying' is uncertain" was muddled · now "as printed du rgod, which gives no sense; probably ngu rgod 'weeping and laughing' (ngu + rgod), a guess" (u. 40).
- gloss ཕྱལ་ཆད་དུ · entry · style · the parenthesis ran the guess and the case ending together · now "(phyal chad, a rare word whose sense is a guess from context, + du 'into')".

- unit 1 · l · style · rtsir ba is read as a guess, but "pressing" had no (?), while the other guessed or uncertain words in `l` carry one ("time(?)", "vivid(?)", "Weeping(?)") · now "pressing(?)".

### Checked and confirmed (no change)

- All 50 units re-read, original → l → i. Pass 1's changes are sound: u. 16 and u. 31 rebuilt i, u. 32 l/i, u. 34 division and i.
- The four misprint notes (u. 6 མཆད, u. 26 ཉམས་ལན, u. 28 མཁ་དོག, u. 50 ཤོར་བདང) use the required form. Every [?] (re u. 11; shig and ལན u. 26; sing nga u. 29; ཅནྡུ u. 45) is called uncertain, and every guess (rtsir ba, 'phar 'phro, skad chung dus, ang, phyal chad, du rgod, rdzogs rim par, rang gi shes nas) is called a guess or uncertain in its note. Gloss and units now agree on each of these.
- The pilot spells goms 'dris as གོམ་འདྲིས, as the note to u. 48 says, and the pilot's u. 26 gives the right and left channels, as the note to u. 37 says.
- The command particle rule in the note to u. 44 is right for the forms it covers: cig after d (gtod cig, mdzod cig), shig after s (sgoms shig, yengs shig). For nyon cig, see the refused findings.
- Known entries checked against their use here and found adequate: གི (covers gi for gis, u. 13); ལམ་གྱིས (u. 37); ཡང / ཀྱང; རིམ་པ (u. 8 "state", within "stage"); དག (u. 33 "correct"); འོང་ངོ; རྩར.

### Findings considered and refused

- u. 2 l "throbbing-remainder" with no (?): `l` gives the parts word for word ('phar + 'phro), which is not a guess. Only the sense drawn from them is a guess, and the note says so. Kept.
- u. 44 nyon cig: after n the expected form would be zhig. But nyon cig is the usual fixed form, the pilot's text has the same kind of cig after other letters, and it is printed so. No note is needed for a reader. Kept.
- u. 13 bzhag te, u. 43 klogs te (te where the rule gives ste): this is the print's usage. The ཏེ gloss now says so, so no unit note is needed.
- Gloss entries that quote a use (e.g. གྲབས "chad pa'i grabs 'about to stop'"): they keep a general sense first and give the phrase as an example, as the master glossary does (བྱ་བ "zhes bya ba: 'so called'"). They are not pinned to one line. Kept.
- ཕྱེད་པར "a form of 'byed": the exact stem of phyed in dbyer mi phyed is not certain (the stems of 'byed are given variously). "A form of" is honest, and it matches the note to u. 30. Kept.
